implemented: Initial A query remainders read original byte windows directly from the canonical prepared snapshot; scalar 128-byte regeneration is not used for those queries.
One opening-batch-local window covers two original columns at D34, capped at 256 MiB, preserving high-to-low blocks and cross-column reuse.
Only the live original prefix is requested from the reader; external zero suffix and private pads retain their original PCS positions.
Canonical byte windows now use the same source-row coverage checks as the initial full-source scanner.
Reader errors terminate the query batch. A changed byte window fails opening against the retained Merkle root.
Base/extension query values are written directly into the returned native base-limb matrix, eliminating the separate full Coefficient matrix.

query_window_fixture.reference: Independent Horner evaluation of the original column polynomial including six nonzero private pads per column.
checks: Each necessary original window is reconstructed once per batch, reused across both columns; final partial window never requests beyond live.
Scalar source callback panics if used; all byte-window query cases complete without calling it.

Out-of-domain/excess queries and byte readers on non-dyadic or extension columns are rejected.
Reader failure on the second window returns an error without reading later windows.
